name: engine_capped_closed_loop_procedural_graph
description: Refactored procedural graph enforcing the 10-order engine ceiling (9 hands max), closed-loop can refilling, uncapped shop arbitrage for wage defense, and calibrated Day 12-13 expansion horizons.

nodes.name: State & Balance Audit
nodes.description: Evaluates net available cash, current step/day/hour, shed fill percentage, wage liabilities, active town shop demand windows, order queue slots, and 96-step oracle supply curves.

nodes.name: Midnight Wage Reserve Defense
nodes.description: Protects payroll for all active hired hands. Enforces emergency liquidation when hour >= 18 and net available cash is below the mandatory wage threshold (hands_count * 120 + 100), channeling sales through active town shops first before open-market dumping.

nodes.name: Terminal Asset Liquidation
nodes.description: Full-spectrum emergency fire sale executing from step 700 to 719. Dumps 100% of shed inventory, livestock feeds, unplanted seeds, and carried produce into cash prior to step 720 game termination.

nodes.name: Shed Headroom Relief
nodes.description: Prevents silent 100/100 harvest discards by preemptively clearing low-margin bulk inventory when shed capacity approaches 96.0, while strictly preserving herd survival feed buffers.

nodes.name: Town Shop Arbitrage & Scarcity Capture
nodes.description: Preemptively matches unlocked town shop contracts (Strawberries, Milk, Tomatoes, Carrots, Eggs) in top priority order slots (slots 1-3) to extract 2.0x-3.5x pricing premiums while preserving a 12-16 unit shop crop buffer.

nodes.name: Early Capital Compounding & 9-Hand Ceiling
nodes.description: Days 0-12 capital reinvestment engine: scales plots to 22-26 and caps workforce strictly at 9 hands (ratio ~2.4 plots/hand) to respect the 10-order engine ceiling while reserving bandwidth for trade orders.

nodes.name: Late Harvest Freeze & Closed-Loop Regrowth Loop
nodes.description: Enacted at Day 12.0 (step 288): permanently halts land expansion and seed purchases, locking hands into a closed-loop harvest-deposit-refill-water cycle to maintain uninterrupted 3-day Strawberry flushes.

nodes.name: Oracle Opponent Front-Run
nodes.description: Monitors 96-step predictive supply curves (TTM forecast) to preemptively dump livestock luxury goods (Wool, Milk) 4-8 turns before competitor gluts crash open market prices (triggered at risk >= 0.50).

nodes.name: Routine Farm & Closed-Loop Execution
nodes.description: Executes physical farm tasks with strict closed-loop can refilling: dispatches workers to Strawberry watering, ready-crop harvesting, immediate well refills upon shed drop-off, and livestock feeding.

attributes.condition: hour >= 18 and day > 0 and step < 700 and net_available_cash < (hands_count * 120 + 100)
attributes.guidance: Immediately halt all land purchases, seed buys, and hiring. Liquidate non-feed inventory immediately. Route sales through active town shops first to capture 2.0x-3.5x premium before dumping on the open market, ensuring cash strictly exceeds (hands_count * 120 + 100) before midnight.
attributes.pitfalls: Never trigger on Day 0 when starting capital ($3,000) is abundant; never liquidate Wheat below minimum livestock survival threshold (6-hour feed buffer); avoid dumping fertilizer on open market for <$30 when high-value goods can be sold to town shops.

attributes.condition: step >= 700 and (shed_used > 0 or carried_inventory > 0 or livestock_feed_count > 0 or unplanted_seeds_count > 0)
attributes.guidance: Execute unconditional fire-sale liquidation across all shed inventory, unplanted seeds, livestock feeds, animal products, and crops. Command hands to deposit carried pack items into the shed and batch-sell 100% of assets into active town shops or open market before step 720.
attributes.pitfalls: Holding unsold inventory past step 719 anticipating higher shop demand; leaving harvested crops inside worker packs during the final simulation tick; retaining animal feed or maintenance reserves into the terminal horizon.

attributes.guidance: Preemptively clear low-margin bulk inventory (excess Fertilizer, Wood, surplus Wheat) to maintain headroom below 96.0 before workers deliver crops, preventing silent 100/100 discards.
attributes.pitfalls: Never evict feed Wheat when animals are hungry (maintain minimum 6-hour feed buffer); do not wait until shed reaches 100 capacity before triggering relief.

attributes.condition: has_unlocked_shops and step < 700 and ((any(s.demands_item_in_shed and s.multiplier >= 2.0 and s.item != 'Tomato' for s in active_shops)) or (day >= 27 and shed.get('Tomato', 0) > 0 and any(s.item == 'Tomato' and s.current_price >= 500 for s in active_shops)) or (shed.get('Strawberry', 0) >= 12 and shop_demands('IceCreamShop', 'Strawberry')) or (shed.get('Milk', 0) >= 12 and shop_demands('BrunchShop', 'Milk')))
attributes.guidance: Fulfill Town Shop contracts to extract 2.0x-3.5x premium prices. Submit shop delivery orders in top order slots (slots 1-3) to ensure priority under the 10-order ceiling. Maintain a 12-16 unit inventory buffer of shop crops (Carrot, Tomato, Egg). Channel bulk Strawberry into Ice Cream Shops and Milk into Brunch Shops. Hoard Tomatoes until Days 27-29 to capture nonlinear supply-exhaustion spikes ($757/unit).
attributes.pitfalls: Never block town shop orders based on cash reserves, as shop orders generate immediate cash; never sell Tomatoes before Day 27 on open market or at low shop multipliers; never hold hoarded Tomatoes past Day 29 Hour 20.

attributes.condition: day <= 12 and step < 700 and (day == 0 or (net_available_cash >= ((hands_count + 1) * 120 + 250) and (hands_count < 9 or cows_count < 9 or sheep_count < 5 or (plots_count < 26 and day < 12.0))))
attributes.guidance: Execute early capital compounding up to Day 12.0: hire up to a strict ceiling of 9 hands (never exceed 9-10 to respect the 10-order engine cap), expand land to 22-26 plots (~2.4 plots/hand ratio), acquire foundation livestock (up to 9 cows, 5 sheep), and establish Strawberry acreage. Ensure cash reserves always exceed wage buffer plus new hire cost before purchasing.
attributes.pitfalls: Hiring 10+ hands, which exhausts order queue capacity and drops market trade orders; buying land or slow seeds after Day 12; expanding capital when net cash dips below the midnight wage buffer.

attributes.guidance: Enforce strict capital freeze: permanently disable plot expansions, tilling, and Strawberry seed purchases. Lock the 9 hired hands into an uninterrupted cyclic watering loop across all established Strawberry plots every tick. Mandate that workers immediately refill watering cans at the well after dropping harvests at the shed, ensuring in-situ watering upon harvest.
attributes.pitfalls: Buying land or slow seeds after Day 12-13, locking cash into unharvestable crops; allowing workers to leave harvested Strawberry plots dry due to empty watering cans; breaking the 3-day regrowth clock.

attributes.condition: oracle_glut_risk >= 0.50 and current_price >= 0.65 * base_price and step < 700
attributes.guidance: Monitor 96-step predictive supply curves (TTM forecast). When opponent glut risk reaches >= 0.50, preemptively liquidate luxury commodities (Wool, Milk) 4-8 turns before competitor mass dumps crash open-market prices to $1.00 floors.
attributes.pitfalls: Premature dumping at risk < 0.50 when prices are stable; dumping after prices have already collapsed; liquidating items currently demanded by active town shops paying 2.0x-3.5x premiums.

attributes.guidance: Dispatch hands in strict sequence: (1) mature crop harvesting, (2) immediate shed deposit, (3) well refill of watering cans, (4) cyclic watering of Strawberry beds, (5) livestock feeding. Keep total dispatched action orders <= 9 to reserve slot 10 for emergency or shop trade execution.
attributes.pitfalls: Submitting >10 total orders per tick; workers carrying harvested crops across multiple ticks instead of immediate delivery; neglecting immediate well refills leading to dry plots.
